title: Gabion node protocol
description: The single source of the message types exchanged between a Gabion application and the Asterisk controller: the conversation connection, the service connection, and the settings the application gives the node. Types for both sides are generated from this file; neither side keeps a hand-written copy. Audio does not travel as these messages: its binary frames are described in audio-frames.md.

ConversationId.description: Stable identifier of a conversation; other modules may keep it.

ParticipantId.description: Identifier of a participant within its conversation.

RecordingId.description: Stable identifier of a recording; other modules may keep it.

SegmentId.description: Identifier of a playback segment, chosen by the application.

PhoneNumber.description: A phone number in E.164 form.

ParticipantState.description: State of a participant who has not left.

Participant.description: A party on the line. The number is absent when the medium has none.

Origin.description: How the conversation came to exist.

oneOf.description: A call from the telephone network to a number of the installation.
A signed-in user's softphone.
A call from a web page, admitted by a one-time pass the application issued.
Started at the application's request; the handler is the one the request named.

Opening.description: Why this conversation connection was opened.

oneOf.description: A new conversation.

connected.description: Groups of participants who hear each other.

oneOf.description: The previous owner is gone. Nothing of its state survives: no playback queues, no subscriptions.

Retention.description: How long a recording is kept; set by whoever starts it.

oneOf.description: Kept until the holder of its identifier releases it.
Deleted when the period ends.

Command.description: What the application asks for. Mirrors the telephony contract one to one.

oneOf.description: Add a participant by dialling. The answer limit is a business rule, not a safeguard.
Let these participants hear each other. Fewer than two, or the same one twice, is rejected with a reason — a command the conversation cannot carry out, not a malformed message.
Take a participant out of whatever group they were connected to.
How long a participant whose connection is lost stays held before they are counted as gone. Zero means lost is gone.
Start receiving what a participant says, as audio frames on this connection.
Queue a segment for a participant. Its audio follows as playback frames carrying the same segment identifier.

CommandOutcome.description: The immediate answer to a command. What came of an accepted command arrives as events.

oneOf.description: Accepted; the new participant already exists and is ringing.
The code is the medium's, kept as it came.

FactOrigin.description: Where a fact about a participant comes from.

Event.description: What happened in the conversation. Mirrors the telephony contract one to one.

oneOf.description: The participant's connection is lost; the conversation waits for them.
Handed to the medium in full. Not 'heard'.
Audio stopped arriving while signalling is alive. A fact, not a diagnosis.
The owner instance is being taken out of service.

ControllerMessage.description: A text message the controller sends on a conversation connection.

protocol.description: Protocol version. An unknown version is refused, never guessed at.

oneOf.description: Always the first message.

ApplicationMessage.description: A text message the application sends on a conversation connection.

oneOf.description: The instance takes the conversation and becomes its owner.
The instance does not take it; the controller tries elsewhere.

id.description: Chosen by the application, unique on this connection.

HandlerId.description: Stable identifier of a conversation handler in the application.

OperatorId.description: Identifier of a telephone operator (a trunk).

PromptId.description: Identifier of a recorded prompt the node can play by itself.

LegId.description: Identifier of a browser call leg, chosen by the application.

Sha256.description: A SHA-256 digest in lowercase hexadecimal.

Network.description: An address range in CIDR form.

SessionDescription.description: Audio parameters a browser offers or receives (SDP). The only thing of the call a browser ever supplies.

DeviceFact.description: A fact a participant's device reports about itself.

BrowserOrigin.description: Whose browser the leg belongs to. The application has already checked the right to call; a browser never names a destination.

oneOf.description: A signed-in user's softphone.
A visitor admitted by a one-time pass the application issued.

Request.description: What the application asks of the node outside any conversation.

oneOf.description: Start a conversation by dialling its first participant. The instance that receives the conversation connection becomes the owner — not necessarily the one that asked.
Create a call leg for a browser. The controller holds the dialogue with Asterisk itself.
A fact from the page; the controller puts it into the conversation's events in order.

RequestOutcome.description: The immediate answer to a request.

Report.description: What the node did while no instance owned a conversation. Nothing the node does on its own goes unreported.

oneOf.description: People connected to each other are being kept together while an owner is looked for.
A participant left with nobody to talk to and nobody in charge.
The node started on the settings it had stored, without the application to confirm them.

NodeMessage.description: A message the controller sends on the service connection.

oneOf.description: Always the first message. The fingerprint is absent when the node has no settings yet.
The node keeps its previous settings and says what is wrong with the new ones.

ApplicationServiceMessage.description: A message the application sends on the service connection.

oneOf.description: The application knows this node and this protocol.
The node should fetch its settings again.

id.description: Chosen by the application, unique on this connection.

port.description: Checked to be a valid port when the settings are applied; a wrong one refuses the settings.

source_networks.description: The only networks calls of this operator are accepted from.

countries.description: Countries this operator carries outbound calls to.

Operator.description: A telephone operator: where its trunk is and what it serves.

allowed_countries.description: Empty means the line makes no outbound calls at all.

Line.description: An outbound line: the number shown, the destinations allowed, the limit of simultaneous calls. The second line of defence — the telephony module has checked the same before asking.

oneOf.description: Softphones of signed-in users.
Calls from web pages admitted by one-time passes.

Fallback.description: What the node does for a caller who was alone with the application when no instance can own the conversation.

oneOf.description: Play the prompt, then hang up.

Entry.description: An entry and its fallback. There is no entry without a fallback.

Prompt.description: A prompt the node fetches by identifier and keeps; the digest tells it when the audio changed.

Settings.description: Everything the node is told in advance. The controller turns it into Asterisk configuration; the application never writes Asterisk's files.
